title: Primitive-to-modern technology pathways: P1-P3 pilot
claim_ceiling: Conceptual graph only. No edge establishes a local process recipe, cost, timeline, safety, or physical reproducibility.

graph_semantics.requires_all: Every listed prerequisite must be qualified.
graph_semantics.requires_any: At least one listed alternative must be qualified; alternatives do not inherit the evidence of each other.
graph_semantics.unknown_prerequisite: The capability is unresolved or blocked; never assume true.
graph_semantics.evidence: Evidence is attached to a specific claim under a specific profile, not to a technology name globally.
graph_semantics.local_use_vs_reproduction: Use, maintenance, repair, replacement-part production, equipment reproduction, reference-chain renewal, and independent transfer are distinct states.
graph_semantics.historical_sequence: Edges are dependency hypotheses, not an assertion that every community must follow a linear sequence.
graph_semantics.physical_authority: This graph grants no authority to purchase, allocate resources, energize equipment, manufacture products, or operate machinery.

evidence_tiers.E1: Credible historical account or specialist reference.
evidence_tiers.E2: Directly documented process with known conditions.
evidence_tiers.E4: Field demonstrated under a bounded local profile.
evidence_tiers.E5: Reproduced by a separately operated node using transferred knowledge and qualified inputs.

sources.author: Lewis Dartnell
sources.title: The Knowledge: How to Rebuild Our World from Scratch
sources.use: Orientation and bibliography seed across agriculture, materials, power, transport, communications, chemistry and scientific knowledge.
sources.limits: Not a validated field manual; technical claims and conditions require specialist verification.

sources.title: Connecting the Scientific and Industrial Revolutions: The Role of Practical Mathematics
sources.use: Research anchor for the relationships between practical mathematics, precision measurement, instrument-making and machine tools.
sources.limits: Historical explanatory evidence; not direct qualification of a modern local production route.

sources.title: The development and use of machine tools in historical perspective
sources.use: Research anchor for machine-tool development, productivity and industrial organization.
sources.limits: Historical overview; does not specify local input, cost or feasibility.

sources.title: UNESCO: Traditional craftsmanship
sources.use: Guidance on the transmission and community context of traditional craft skills.
sources.limits: Not a technical process specification; community consent and knowledge restrictions must be respected.

sources.title: UNESCO: Transmission
sources.use: Guidance on knowledge and skills transfer across generations.
sources.limits: Not a technical process specification; local practitioners remain active knowledge holders.

nodes.label: Observation, counting, shared measures and recordkeeping
open_questions: Which local measures are repeatable and comparable?
Who maintains records and teaches the practice?

nodes.label: Local resource, tool, energy and skill census
open_questions: Are inventories observed or merely reported?
Which seasonal, ecological and access constraints apply?

nodes.label: Manual tools, workholding and basic repair
open_questions: Which tools and materials are actually present?
Which tasks require an unrepresented specialist skill?

nodes.label: Bounded material shaping, joining and transformation routes
open_questions: Which resource and material grades are verified?
What energy, waste and environmental limits apply?
Which transformation routes are locally demonstrated?

nodes.label: Repeatable measurement and reference-artifact continuity
open_questions: What is the uncertainty of the reference?
How is the reference checked and renewed?
Which claims require external calibration?

nodes.label: Renewable cutting tools, jigs, fixtures and workholding
open_questions: What material properties and tolerances are required?
Can wear surfaces and cutting edges be renewed?

nodes.label: A qualified useful-work drive and mechanical transmission
open_questions: Is the resource seasonal?
Are bearings, lubrication, structures and guards available?
Can safe operating limits be established?

nodes.label: A bounded machine-tool capability with inspectable output
open_questions: Which parts and tolerance classes are demonstrated?
Which spindles, slides, bearings, motors and controls remain external?
What calibration and inspection chain is required?

nodes.label: Bounded electricity generation or conversion capability
open_questions: What conductor, insulation, magnetic-material, bearing and protection requirements apply?
Can output and fault conditions be measured safely?
What remains import-dependent?

nodes.label: Safe, bounded electrical service for selected loads
open_questions: Are protection, insulation, grounding, storage and inspection prerequisites satisfied?
Which dependencies are external?

nodes.label: Use of a computer or communications module
open_questions: What power, storage, interface, language, security and maintenance constraints apply?
What fails if networking is absent?

nodes.label: Qualified diagnostics and repair of selected electronic assemblies
open_questions: What test equipment and schematics are available?
Which components and packages can actually be replaced?
What electrostatic and electrical protections are needed?

nodes.label: Advanced semiconductor-device manufacturing capability
open_questions: Ultra-pure materials, contamination control, vacuum, deposition/etch, lithography, process chemicals, water, metrology, yield and supply requirements remain unmapped in this pilot.

nodes.label: Versioned, duplicateable technical knowledge packet and training pathway
open_questions: Are diagrams, worked examples, failure modes, units, revisions, rights and training/assessment methods included?
Can people use this offline?

profiles.notes: Initial nodes are declared scenario inputs for the pilot; their presence must be justified for a real profile.
Possession of equipment is not proof that it is operable, maintainable, repairable, or renewable.
Represents selected external/modern modules without assuming local production of the complete upstream industrial system.

required_future_tests: Changing local resource/energy/skill constraints must not rewrite source claims.
Removing a required prerequisite must block closure unless a declared qualified alternative exists.
An imported module can count as usable only under its declared availability and qualification evidence; it must not count as locally reproducible.
The semiconductor node must remain explicitly unresolved until its high-purity process and toolchain dependencies are modeled.
All present E0 nodes must stay E0 until claim-specific evidence is admitted.
The independent verifier must reject forged transition receipts and missing critical dependency tokens.
